solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hot tunes please old setter

parts.note: H is the usual abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
airs are tunes or melodies
pray, as in 'pray be seated', is an old-fashioned way of saying please

explanation.surface: A request that someone hot and bothered stop singing and humour an elderly person who sets puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old setter' reads as an elderly crossword compiler, but 'old' belongs with 'please' and the definition is just 'setter', something that sets a hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A lacquer sprayed on hair holds a style in place, so it is literally something that sets hair.

clue.text: Erica has no longer to conserve energy

indicators.note: to conserve something is to keep it safe within, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: hath is the archaic form of has, no longer in current use
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone called Erica has stopped saving energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Erica reads as a woman's name, but it is the botanical genus of heathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the Latin genus name for heathers, the low shrubs that grow on moorland.

clue.text: Their angle can be adjusted to be identical, possibly

indicators.note: adjusted means altered or rearranged, so the letters of these words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A geometry or engineering note: tweak the angle until two parts match.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that can be swapped for one another are likely to be the same, hence 'possibly' qualifying identical.

clue.text: Family member working in US city in southwest

indicators.note: the second in says the preceding letters sit inside the compass abbreviation

parts.note: SW is the compass abbreviation for southwest
on means working or operating, as a machine is on
taken as written
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A relative has a job in an American city in the southwest of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter's husband becomes a relative by marriage, one kind of member of the wider family.

clue.text: To check vehicle, engineer started lapping ring

indicators.note: lapping means wrapping around, so the rearranged letters enclose the round letter
to engineer is to contrive or rework, so the letters of started are rearranged

parts.note: a ring is round, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: An engineer tests a car by starting it and driving it round a circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineer' turns STARTED into RADTEST, and 'lapping' puts O inside it after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a car out on the road to see how it performs is the standard way of trying it out.

clue.text: I agree: food fit for an ambitious young man

parts.note: yup is a casual way of saying yes, I agree
a pie is an example of food

explanation.surface: Someone nods along that a certain dish suits a go-getting young fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1980s word for a young urban professional describes a career-driven, upwardly mobile person.

clue.text: Soprano's target, maybe, capturing current theme?

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so the note's letters enclose the electrical symbol

parts.note: top C is a high note a soprano might aim for
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Is a soprano's goal to seize on whatever subject is in vogue?
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject of a discussion or piece of writing, a near synonym.

clue.text: Dealer turned up paintings from the communist era?

indicators.note: turned up in a down entry means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: red art would be art from a communist (red) period

explanation.surface: An art dealer discovers a cache of Soviet-era paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer is someone who buys and sells goods, a merchant.

clue.text: Left instruction involving gown in motel, say

indicators.note: involving means wrapping in, so the gown sits between the two other pieces

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a word can be an order, as in 'give the word'
a manteau is an old loose gown or cloak

explanation.surface: A note left for staff about a dressing gown in a roadside hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Motel blends motor and hotel, a classic example of a word made by fusing two others.

clue.text: Order to teenager that's essential for chip maker

definitions.meaning: the familiar parental command to tidy up one's bedroom
microchips are made in a dust-free controlled environment of that name

explanation.surface: A command shouted at a messy teenager doubles as a requirement for a semiconductor factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Parents tell teens to tidy their bedrooms; chip fabs need a dust-free sealed workspace by the same name.

clue.text: Soldier meets retiring girl, dish perhaps

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of ant

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A soldier meets a shy girl, perhaps over a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite dish is one example of an aerial for receiving signals.

clue.text: Public relations broadcast that is plain

parts.note: to air something is to broadcast it
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A PR broadcast that is plain and unadorned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' reads as an adjective, but it is the noun: a flat grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a wide expanse of flat grassland, the North American kind of plain.

clue.text: Horse unseats one big bird

indicators.note: unseats means throws off, so the letter for one is removed

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A horse throws its rider, a large bird looking on.
explanation.definitionFit: The grey wading bird with long legs and neck is a large bird of rivers and marshes.

clue.text: Large family member goes to welcome British crew

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so one piece receives the other

parts.note: goes, as in has a go, means tries
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: A member of a big family goes off to greet a British crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribe can be seen as a very large extended family, so one of its people fits.

clue.text: He brings up English cases to run through

indicators.note: cases means encloses, as a box holds its contents

parts.note: to bring up children is to rear them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man raises English legal cases to go over them.
explanation.definitionFit: To run through a play or speech is to practise it before performance.

clue.text: Steep watercourse engulfs European dog

parts.note: to ret flax or hemp is to steep it in water

indicators.note: engulfs means swallows up, so the watercourse holds the next letter

parts.note: a river is a watercourse

explanation.surface: A steep stream swallows up a European's dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' looks like an adjective for the watercourse, but it is the verb meaning soak.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun dog bred to fetch shot game is a common breed type, such as the Labrador or golden.

clue.text: Back a selection of good numbers to release

indicators.note: Back says the hidden letters are read backwards
a selection of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Supporting a handful of fine songs to put out.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten or untie something is to set it free.

clue.text: Hawk's target before long includes PM

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so the time word wraps around the statesman

parts.note: soon means before long
Pitt, elder or younger, was a British prime minister

explanation.surface: A hawk's prey will soon include the prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' reads as the bird or a warmonger, but here it is the verb: to clear the throat and spit.
explanation.definitionFit: To hawk is to cough up phlegm, and a bowl provided for spitting is where it should land.

clue.text: Charge printed on back of envelope

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: stamped means printed or impressed

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A charge marked on the rear of an envelope, like postage due.
explanation.definitionFit: A headlong rush of a herd or crowd is a charge, as in a cavalry charge.

clue.text: Churchill for one smelt bad with no lead on

indicators.note: with no lead on means losing the first letter, the front of the word

parts.note: stank means smelt bad

explanation.surface: Winston Churchill reeked, with no dog lead on him.
explanation.walkthrough: Churchill reads as the statesman, but the Churchill was a British armoured vehicle of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Churchill was a British infantry armoured fighting vehicle of World War II, named after the prime minister.

clue.text: Raises squad to cross river nearer its source

parts.note: ups, as in ups the price, means raises

indicators.note: to cross here means to straddle, so the squad's letters sit either side

parts.note: a squad is a team

explanation.surface: A squad is raised to ford a river near where it rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Going against the current takes you towards the head of a river, where it begins.

clue.text: Make still from bits of alembic I discarded

indicators.note: bits of says the word is broken into pieces and rearranged
discarded says the letter that follows is thrown out of the pool before rearranging

explanation.surface: A chemist makes a still out of parts of an old alembic.
explanation.walkthrough: An alembic is an old distilling apparatus, which makes 'still' look like the noun; it is the verb, to calm.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a sailing ship motionless for lack of wind, or more generally to calm, is to make it still.

clue.text: Asian dish, cold, very cold

parts.note: a balti is a South Asian curry cooked in a wok-like pot
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A curry served cold, unpleasantly so.
explanation.definitionFit: Baltic is informal British slang for freezing weather, after the icy northern sea.

clue.text: Popular English stage worker perhaps lacking grace

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a leg is a stage of a journey or race
a worker ant is one kind of ant

explanation.surface: A well-liked English stagehand who happens to be clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage worker' reads as one theatre phrase, but splits into a leg of a journey and an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without elegance or poise is awkward and clumsy.

clue.text: Display university books on way to work?

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the first pieces follow the method

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a way of working
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A university puts books on show on the route to the office.
explanation.definitionFit: To mount an exhibition is to put it on display.

clue.text: Stunner took exam again, having been laid up

indicators.note: laid up in a down entry means the letters are put upward, so read backwards

parts.note: resat means took an exam a second time

explanation.surface: A beauty retook an exam after being ill in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stunner' looks like praise for a beauty; it is a stun gun.
explanation.definitionFit: The electroshock weapon fires darts that incapacitate a person, literally a stunning device.

clue.text: Dynamic six support conservationists

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
a bra is a supporting undergarment
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: Six energetic people back the conservationists.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of energy and life, lively and vigorous.

clue.text: Old and anxious but not very demanding

indicators.note: but not says the following letter is left out

parts.note: nervous means anxious

explanation.surface: An elderly person, nervous but not excessively demanding.
explanation.definitionFit: A burdensome task is heavy and taxing, making great demands.

clue.text: It may indicate a cold part of house, I hear

indicators.note: I hear signals a word that sounds like the one given

parts.note: a room is part of a house

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a draughty part of the house means they will catch a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: Watery discharge from the nose or eyes is a symptom of a common cold.

clue.text: One who competes to deceive nurse

parts.note: to con is to deceive
one who tends the sick is a tender

explanation.surface: A competitor sets out to trick a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: A rival in a race or contest is a challenger competing for the prize.
